cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to God's people in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7). He's just told them sin shall not be their master, because they're not under law, but under grace (Romans 6:14). So he asks the question somebody was bound to ask: "Shall we sin because we are not under law, but under grace?"

cards.question: Paul asks if we should keep sinning since we're under grace and not under law. What's his answer?

cards.text: Friend, that's like me hearing every burnt batch is forgiven and cranking every oven to MAXIMUM just to celebrate. Then Paul explains with a picture he says they should already know: slaves and masters.

cards.question: In Paul's picture of slaves and masters, who does he say you're a slave to?

answers.text: The one you were born under

cards.question: Paul says that besides being a slave to sin or to obedience, there's a third option: offering yourself to no master at all.
Paul says each master takes you somewhere. Where does he say being a slave to sin leads?

cards.text: Then Paul stops to give thanks to God. These folks in Rome once were slaves to sin, but that's not where their story stayed.

cards.question: The believers in Rome were once slaves to sin. What does Paul thank God that they did?

answers.text: Kept every part of the law
Worked to earn their own freedom

cards.question: Paul says that once the believers in Rome were set free from sin, they became slaves to righteousness.

cards.text: Then Paul says, "I am speaking in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh." I respect that, friend, because when anybody explains anything to me, I need it in cookie terms or I'm LOST.

cards.question: Paul tells the believers in Rome to offer the parts of their body in slavery to righteousness now. Which parts does he mean?

answers.text: The same parts they once gave to impurity
Only the parts never used for sin
Only the parts the law calls clean

cards.text: Then Paul looks back: when they were slaves to sin, they were free of obligation to righteousness. That's like me bragging I'm free from following any recipe, friend, which means I'm FREE to make dough nobody will touch.

cards.question: Paul asks the believers in Rome what fruit they reaped back then from some of the things they did. How does he say they feel about those things now?

cards.text: And Paul says plainly where those things end: "The outcome of those things is death."
Then come two words I'd stamp on every cookie I own: but now. Paul says they've been set free from sin and have become slaves to God, and the fruit they reap leads to holiness.

cards.question: Paul says that for those who've been set free from sin and become slaves to God, the outcome is the same as it was before.

cards.text: Then Paul lands the whole thing with one line, and it starts on payday: "For the wages of sin is death…"

cards.question: Paul says the wages of sin is death, but the ___ of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
